evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: 說文釋形; 釋義; 零 character record
evidence.text: The entry gives the Great Xu Shuowen reading 餘雨也。从雨，令聲 and, in the Duan Yucai edition, 徐雨也。从雨，霝聲. It also lists 零雨其濛 from the Shijing and later senses including falling, scattered or residual quantities, and a numeric zero. These dictionary examples are not a dated chronology of every semantic transition.
evidence.title: A04475 零 - 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫, Chinese University of Hong Kong
evidence.text: The entry analyzes 零 as 雨 semantic plus 令 phonetic, glossing it as the falling of rain, snow, frost, or dew. It cites the Shijing phrase 靈雨既零 with Mao commentary 零，落也, then Chu Ci use for withering, Hou Hanshu use for death or old age, a Wenxuan use for tears, Song Bao Zheng use for a remainder, and a modern literary use for zero. This is evidence for separate attested extensions but the page does not date the compositions or surviving witnesses.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 零

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫, Chinese University of Hong Kong
evidence.field: 甲骨文解說; 霝 entry
evidence.text: The page explains that the graphs of 霝 have been variously analyzed as 雨 plus two or three 口, interpreted as abundant rain, fine rain, or vessels receiving rain. It says these proposals lack strong evidence and that the graph’s original referent remains unresolved. It separately reports oracle-bone uses mostly as personal names and bronze uses with senses such as good, including loans/readings written 靈 or 令. This does not establish that 零 itself is attested in oracle-bone inscriptions.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 雨部 / 霝

evidence.source: Treccani, Enciclopedia della Scienza e della Tecnica
evidence.text: The article distinguishes empty positions in counting-rod notation from a written round zero sign. It reports the commonly cited appearance of the round symbol in Qin Jiushao’s 1247 Shushu jiuzhang, while noting round zero symbols in some twelfth-century calendar texts. This evidence concerns the round symbol/zero notation and does not establish that 零 was then used as the graph for zero.
evidence.title: La scienza in Cina: dai Qin-Han ai Tang. La matematica

gaps: No reliable ancient inscription image or specific dated oracle-bone/bronze attestation for 零 was verified; do not repeat the dossier’s claim that oracle-bone 零 depicts raindrops.

The Shuowen Great Xu and Duan Yucai readings disagree between 令聲 and 霝聲. The consulted sources do not establish whether the difference arose from textual transmission, graphic interpretation, or corruption.

The phonetic analysis is supported by dictionary tradition, and the dossier’s Baxter–Sagart data reports one 令 reading matching 零 (*[r]ˤiŋ, MC leng), but 令 has multiple readings. The component’s exact intended reading in this compound is not independently certain from this evidence.

Both character-specific official Unihan pages were inaccessible. The local dossier’s current Mandarin data is therefore not treated as verified click-through evidence; 令’s current Mandarin row remains especially unresolved.

The Shijing citations support a rain/falling sense and later dictionaries attest extensions to falling, withering, tears, fragments/remainders, and zero, but the consulted references do not date each semantic transition or prove a single linear progression.

No accessible primary source established the claim that Li Ye used 零 as a zero placeholder in 1248. Treccani discusses round zero symbols and empty positions, which are graphically and historically distinct claims.

No graph corruption or whole-graph phonetic-loan analysis was established. 零 is treated as a sound-semantic compound in dictionary accounts; the source-word issue for a whole-graph loan therefore does not arise.
A usable directly rendered Xiaoxuetang 零 glyph could not be retrieved. The only proposed image candidate is Commons’ later digital seal-script redraw; no ancient artifact photograph was verified.
The recurring dictionary and dataset reuse terms were not assessed for bulk extraction; no local extract recommendation is made.

items.period: Seal-script form as transmitted in the Shuowen tradition; modern vector illustration uploaded 2014
items.caption: A modern vector redraw of 零 in the seal-script style associated with Shuowen; it shows the traditional 雨 and 令 components, not an excavated inscription.
items.alt: Monochrome outlined seal-script character 零, digitally redrawn.
items.selection_reason: Provides a reusable illustration of the dictionary-preserved seal form and the two components central to the supported analysis. It is not evidence for an oracle-bone form or an artifact’s date.
items.rights: Wikimedia Commons page states the vector representation is public domain; the description also notes courtesy/permission associated with the cited Sears source. Treat as a modern redraw, not an ancient artifact photograph.

limitations.text: The proposed seal glyph is a modern digital vector redraw of a received script form, not a photograph or facsimile of an excavated ancient inscription.
No Xiaoxuetang 零 image is proposed because no exact character-specific record or rendered glyph URL could be retrieved, despite the database's stated CC0 terms for queried glyph images.
